title: Yonto plugin manifest
$comment: Strict here and lenient on a device: an author's typo is refused where it can still be fixed, and a television drops a key it does not know so a manifest from a later contract still loads. The same holds for configSchema's items and their options.

allOf.$comment: A plugin whose hosts come out of its own configuration document declares that, and then nothing checks where it goes — so a list of hosts in its manifest would be one nobody reads. Every other plugin's list is enforced, empty or not; empty means it reaches only what the viewer configured.

probeCategory.$comment: Read by `doctor` and by nothing on a device, which drops a key it does not know — so it costs no contract version.
probeCategory.description: The id of the category `doctor` lists and pages, when the first one would not exercise paging. Absent, it takes the first.

allowedHosts.description: Hosts this plugin may reach, before the host adds any the viewer configured. Empty is legal and means the plugin reaches nothing on its own — which is what a source pointed at a server only its owner can name (a Jellyfin box, a 仓 config URL) declares.

runsFetchedCode.$comment: Nothing checks this and nothing can: `lint` reads a plugin's own source, and code a plugin downloads at run time is not in it. So it is a declaration an author makes, the install dialog repeats it, and its absence means only that nobody said so — never that the plugin does not. Absent is false so a manifest written before this existed goes on meaning what it always meant, which is also why the dialog can only ever add a line rather than withdraw one. See contracts/content-source-http.md's "A source that runs code it fetched".
runsFetchedCode.description: Whether this plugin downloads further code at run time and executes it — an XPTV index names a JavaScript file per catalog. A self-declaration, repeated on the install dialog, that no host verifies.

playbackTokens.$comment: Nothing in a plugin's source says it will return a `pan` option, so this is the only way a host can place the floor — the same shape as catalogsAreRemote and runsFetchedCode. Absent is false, which is what every source written before this one was: every option it answers carries a `stream`. A host too old to understand a token would decode such an option with `stream` required and fail the whole title, which is why this is a version gate rather than a key an older host drops. See contracts/content-source-http.md's "A source whose option is not a URL yet".
playbackTokens.description: Whether this source may answer a playback option that is not a URL yet — a `pan` share for the host to open, or a `track` for its own getStream to redeem.

catalogsAreRemote.$comment: Absent is false, and false is the rule every source written before this one kept: getSubSources answers from what the source already knows. A host meeting this on a manifest it is too old to understand drops it and asks the way it always did, which is the behaviour that was there before rather than a new failure. See contracts/content-source-http.md's "A source whose catalog list is itself remote".
catalogsAreRemote.description: Whether this source's library list lives somewhere it has to go and read — an XPTV or TVBox index at a URL. Such a source may fetch inside getSubSources, and the host owes it a visible wait over an empty picker in exchange.

provides.$comment: Required here and not on a device. A plugin bundled before this field existed must stay installable, and `source-type` is what every such plugin already was — so the contract makes an author say it and a host that meets a manifest without it reads the conservative answer rather than refusing the plugin.
provides.description: Whether this plugin is a source, or a kind of source. `source` means it knows its own address and is a source for as long as it is on the box. `source-type` means the viewer names the instance — a Jellyfin lives only where its owner put it — so installing it offers to set one up, and there may be several.

handles.$comment: No contract version: an app that predates it drops the key, and a handler is still an ordinary source-type plugin there. `lint` holds the names to contracts/yonto-types/ and the plugin to the types it claims. See docs/design/2026-09-23-the-app-reads-every-index.md, *Types*.
handles.description: The Yonto types this plugin reads an index entry of: a bare name with a file in contracts/yonto-types/, or somebody else's reverse-DNS name (`io.github.someone.alist`).

items.$comment: A cookieLogin's session belongs to the host: it is kept beside the profile, attached by yonto.fetch to this capability's own site per redirect hop, and never handed to the plugin. `writesTo` — the config field a capability used to write it into, where the plugin's own JavaScript read it — went with that, and additionalProperties refuses it rather than ignoring it. See docs/design/2026-09-20-the-host-holds-the-session.md. A browserCheck names where a plugin may send the viewer to pass a site's browser check, by `url` for one https site or by `fromConfig` for any public https site a hostsFromConfig plugin reaches; what it wins is the host's in the same way. See docs/design/2026-09-23-a-challenge-the-viewer-clears.md. A linkLogin is a sign-in the viewer finishes on a phone, run by the host for a service contracts/link-logins.json names; the credential it wins is the host's and never reaches the plugin. See docs/design/2026-09-24-a-code-the-viewer-links.md. pointerLogin was a name with nothing behind it and is refused rather than accepted and ignored.

allOf.$comment: A linkLogin names a service in contracts/link-logins.json and nothing else: where its sign-in and its server list are, what their answers look like and which field is a credential are the host's to know, so no manifest can name them.
